item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
+ In which I attack old skips.
- I know the author is inactive, just roll with the 'you's

fifteen (15) minutes | twenty-five (25) square centimetres | One (1) standard sheet

I guess this is a stylistic choice, but bluhhh. I know what numbers are, you don't have to reiterate what the hell a one is.

250 K (-23°C)

I understand now (thanks to 19) that Kelvin is just as standard as Celsius, but if you've already used Kelvin previously why is it suddenly also giving the Celsius equivalent? It feels needlessly inconstant, and the article should probably just stick to one measurement.

SCP-754-2

One can deduce that -2 are actual, live instances. But it's never explicitly stated. The base 754 designation basically describes -2, since I somehow doubt -1 cares about water and such.

any root fragments left intact will be stimulated and [DATA EXPUNGED] | [DATA EXPUNGED] | [DATA EXPUNGED]

Wow that is some crap expunging.

class A amnesiac

Forget the drugs, throw Uncle Larry at him!

Addendum 754-02

Shouldn't this actually be in the containment procedures? Plus, I mean… how? This invalidates the previous description, doesn't it? Somebody's arm is not whitespace. This development would be a big deal, and it's just sitting at the end of the document as a single sentence. Was it supposed to be a wham line of sorts? If so, felt kinda weak.

For everything above, I downvoted. The idea of a drawn flower that grows on paper, and then eventually goes critical and starts budding in real life sounds kinda neat. But it feels poorly executed, and there's not much beyond the anomaly itself.

item.title: CALL FOR REVIEW
item.content:encoded:
EDIT: Sorry for the confusion. I am not staff, but I am working for the Rewrite Team in doing this call for review.

This is a call for review on this article, which has been selected as needing more attention.

The idea of a plant that can grow in crazy and extreme environments is not something that's just limited to the Foundation. Predatory plants live in marshy swamps where they lack the nitrogen that they need for survival. Certain species of plants live in tough environments where nutrients are scarce, and where they are barely able to eke out a living.

That's part of why this article is so cool. It's a plant that propagates itself through paper and illustrations. It gives you a great mental image of a slowly creeping menace that is able to outgrow practically anything, and with the ability to take over so many environments. We see real life examples of invasive species, and this is just a logical step to take it over to the Foundation. Invasive species have this touch of sci-fi to them; a species that lands in a foreign place and rapidly seizes it. It fits in nicely with alien invasion tropes, or simple human xenophobia.

That said, there's quite a few issues with this article, mostly in the realm of clarity of description and a few tonal errors due to the fact that this is something from pre-Mass Edit days.

The best way to sum up one of the main issues of this article is this comment:

Should there not be a physical description of 754-2, or at least some description of how it's similar to or different from 754-1?

-Quikngruvn

The first time I read this article, I had to do a couple of rereads as I searched for what exactly the difference between 754-2 and the regular garden variety1 of 754 was. Then I realized that there is no description. This whole article goes by, and 754-2 is never truly defined, leaving the reader unsure of what exactly is going on here, and questioning if naming a separate 754-2 is even necessary. If the difference between the two, as the author suggests is:

I had sort of figured that the general description applies to both forms, except that -1 is drawn and -2 is live. I can try to make that more clear, if it's needed.

-karajade

…then shouldn't this be stated in the article itself? Another issue raised is:

I'm a little confused as to the "volitional figures fighting against it" bit. Does this mean that static figures in the scene will change to new illustrations or that they actually animate like Cassie? What happens if we try to erase a pencil illustration partway during the process?

-Drewbear

Again, what does this mean in the article? If this plant grew into the Mona Lisa, would la Gioconda herself start attacking 754? It adds an interesting dimension to the paper plant2 but it's not really fleshed out enough for it to flow smoothly with the rest of the article.

Other smaller errors are slight snagging points throughout the article. The writing is often awkward throughout the article, requiring re-reads and more reader interpretation to figure out what exactly the author was thinking. Some fixes to improve clarity would be greatly appreciated here, in order to make it simply easier to read.

The final issues are more tonal/site culture based. The [DATA EXPUNGED] in the last few sections seems tacked on for added mystery value without actually seeming well-rooted. It's a plant that [DATA EXPUNGED]. The lead-up to this point heavily contrasts with the sudden addition of the mysterious expunging. It somewhat detracts from the article's focus as an invasive plant that is able to tackle lots of terrains.

Another sticking point is the hiring of the office worker at the end. In current protocol, this wouldn't happen. It was a vastly different time when this SCP was originally written, and I can't imagine this being used in an article now, unless there was a very good reason to do so. Hiring an office worker just because he/she happened to be dealing with the plant is a little iffy for a lot of people, myself included. Putting them in charge of containment goes a step too far.

All in all, it's still a good article. The idea is cool, and the execution is done fairly well. However, it's in need of some serious clarifications to improve the overall focus and cohesiveness of the article, and could use some updating to suit the times.

I highly encourage that all of you think about it.

Footnotes
1. My sincerest apologies for the pun.
2. More apologies for the punning.

item.title: Review
item.content:encoded:
1) "Addendum 754-02" needs to be moved to the containment section.

2) Too much expungement.

3) The containment procedure's don't say what the hand drawn illustration should be. The illustration should be of something really big, like a mountain, with no nearby objects showing (or it could even be an illustration of an entire planet, if that would work). Since the spread across paper varies with scale, this will slow down its spread across the paper.

3b) The hand drawn illustration should depict a scene with temperatures just above 150 K, to make it spread even more slowly.

4) The containment procedure should mention something about a minimum Psychic Resistance Scale that all containment staff interacting with the -1 version must meet.
